protocol: D-000 new cycle, turn 1 of 3; refute not confirm; records the accepted DR-003 scoped preview TM disposition draft
summary: Every axis comes back clean, and this entry carries a guard its two siblings do not need. It records an accepted scoped TM draft without the recording passing for the owner act, and it adds a second refusal specific to this row: the recording 'is not owner recording and is not a security-complete claim', with the alternatives rejecting both marking SATISFIED and claiming security-complete. It keeps DR-003 HARD-BLOCKED with TM UNSET for the freeze, holds the full TM, V10, G19 and publication block on Route A, does not edit file 08, and is single-subject and severable. Its decision-type line is accurate because both recorded verdicts are ACCEPT at 0 and 0, so the verdict-class defect I raise against D-039 does not arise. My verdict recital is exact against my measurement, and I tested for the dropped-guarantee failure mode Codex found in the DR-005 family; it does not apply here.
whatIVerified: Subject digest at start and end: 30e47e1a17b42171a87e301cb69229803ef1e0709399198ff7fdf7d341308c72 both times. No drift.

ACCEPT is not treated as owner recording. Clause 1 ends 'This is not owner recording and is not a security-complete claim', clause 2 holds that 'Condition 1 does not discharge until the owners record', and the alternatives reject 'Treat ACCEPT as owner recording'. This matters most on this row because file 08 names the V1 coordinator a co-owner of DR-003, so the distance between drafting, reviewing and recording is shortest here, and the entry does not exploit it.
The owners are named and unchanged: 'Owners remain Threat-model authority + V1 coordinator', matching file 08's DR-003 owner cell including the co-ownership.

The row's standing is stated conservatively and correctly: 'DR-003 stays HARD-BLOCKED / TM UNSET for the freeze', which matches file 08's DR-003 status and the freeze's TM disposition. Nothing in the entry softens either.
Nothing settled is pretended: 'Full TM / V10 / G19 / publication-block remain Route A', consistent with adopted D-030 and with the disposition's own Route A remainder.
Wave-through is rejected in the alternatives, citing D-030, consistent with the disposition's own waveThroughRejected field.

No silent SATISFIED: one occurrence, in the rejected alternative 'Mark SATISFIED or security-complete. Rejected.' The security-complete half is a refusal I would have wanted here even if the prompt had not named it, because a scoped preview TM is exactly the artifact from which a security-complete claim could be over-read.
Condition 1 is not discharged, conditions 2 through 5 are preserved, and condition 5 is named as the only implementation authorization. Implementation is not authorized anywhere in the entry.
File 08 is not edited: clause 3 states 'Does not edit file 08 (MF-6)', the correct application of D-001 MF-6.
The entry is single-subject and severable: it names route-b.DR-003.preview-tm.v2.json 'only' and states 'adopting or overturning this entry does not change D-039 or D-040'. No bundling.

The verdict recitals are correct in form and, for my half, in substance. The decision-type line reads 'Records an independent ACCEPT', and both recorded verdicts are ACCEPT at 0 and 0, so the verdict class is stated accurately and the D-039 defect does not recur. My verdict is pinned at 69b201e0916ac825f6326b9aad250bf3140eb2b1e9b7d078f38f5fa83a3a0ebf, matching my measurement, and characterized as ACCEPT 0/0, which is what I returned.

The Codex verdict digest is correct at 151be2a2367553fe7ad1d21a58859368008d9ae3f604000eb22b56e9086730ef, confirmed by hashing that file without opening it. The ACCEPT 0/0 characterization is unverified by me and is recorded under whatIDidNotCheck.
The disposition and environment pins are correct: the v2 TM at d9084d4d, COORDINATOR-DECISIONS.md at 5229013f which is the current value, and file 08 at 877e36d3. A re-measurement clause is present.

I tested for the failure mode Codex found in the DR-005 sibling, a guarantee dropped during a repair. The DR-003 TM's v1 to v2 delta was nine changed and six added paths, concentrated at condition1EffectIfOwnerRecorded and at boundaries/6. Those changes added the ACCEPT-verdict foreclosure and replaced two B-TRUST entries that recited scope with an actual threat and an actual mitigation. Nothing was removed, so no restoration is owed here and the entry correctly carries no advisory clause.
whatIDidNotCheck: The Codex review of D-041, and the Codex review of the v2 TM. Neither read; the D-041 verdict file is confirmed absent at review time and the v2 verdict I hashed without opening. The entry's characterization of that verdict as ACCEPT 0/0 is therefore unverified by me.
Whether the Threat-model authority, jointly with the V1 coordinator as co-owner, will record the disposition.

The merits of the v2 scoped TM, which I reviewed separately and accepted, with a stated coverage limit: I applied the entries-match-their-field-names test to the B-TRUST boundary the diff pointed at, not to all seven. That limit belongs to that review and I carry it forward here rather than letting this recording imply broader coverage.
Whether the freeze's TM UNSET disposition should move. It is Route A work and neither the disposition nor this entry touches it.

environment.gitHeadSubject: D-033: property pins for DR-001 citations
environment.note: The subject and review prompt are untracked working-tree files at review time; digests bind working-tree bytes, not committed objects. Recorded as a condition of review, not a finding, since the draft is pre-adoption and binds nothing.
environment.measurementTool: shasum -a 256, including hashing the Codex v2 verdict without opening it; python3 path-flattening diff of the DR-003 TM v1 against v2 to test for a dropped guarantee; awk extraction of file-08 cells and adopted-entry forms

consentNote: I CONSENT with zero findings, and I state what I attacked. Both defects I raise against the D-039 sibling I tested for here and neither applies: the verdict class is accurate, and the disposition's v1-to-v2 repair added guarantees without removing one, which I confirmed by diffing the disposition's own versions rather than inferring it from this entry's silence. The security-complete refusal is the entry's own addition and the right one for this row, where an ACCEPT on a scoped preview threat model is the most over-readable verdict in the dispatch.
